description: Congresswoman Lisa McClain (MI-10) is seeking highly motivated, detail-oriented, and energetic applicants for a full-time paid internship in Washington, D.C. Intern responsibilities include answering phones, researching legislation, attending virtual hearings and briefings, answering constituent letters on various issues before the House, and assisting in various administrative tasks as needed. As a result, the intern will learn about the legislative process and the many other functions of a congressional office. Congresswoman McClain supports students requesting credit for their internship through their school or university. This is an in-person internship. Applicants must be willing to wear a mask and adhere to strict social distancing and sanitation guidelines. District and Michigan ties are encouraged but not required.
responsibilities: Answering constituent letters on various issues before the House
Assisting in various administrative tasks as needed
qualifications: Strong written and verbal communication skills
Ability to manage multiple tasks
Willingness to learn
Highly motivated, detail-oriented, and energetic
District and Michigan ties are encouraged but not required
how_to_apply: Email your resume to jacquelyn.eubanks@mail.house.gov and include "Internship Application—Summer 2021" or "Internship Application—Fall 2021" in the subject line. No drop-ins.

description: The Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on the Western Hemisphere, Civilian Security, and Trade – chaired by Congressman Albio Sires (D-NJ) – is seeking one full-time intern for Spring 2021. The intern will work closely with subcommittee staff while learning the inner workings of Congress and the legislative process. The internship is a U.S. based remote eligible position and will become available first week of March 2021. Undergraduate or graduate school students and recent alumni interested in foreign affairs and Western Hemisphere policy are encouraged to apply. Spanish, French or Portuguese proficiency preferred but not required.
responsibilities: Providing administrative and research support to staff
Assisting with subcommittee hearings and briefings
Attending virtual events and writing memorandum for staff
qualifications: Enthusiastic, professional, hard-working, and detail-oriented
Strong writing and communication skills
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced work environment
Undergraduate or graduate school student or recent alumnus interested in foreign affairs and Western Hemisphere policy
Spanish, French or Portuguese proficiency preferred but not required
how_to_apply: Send a one-page resume and cover letter to WHEMjobs@gmail.com with the subject line "Spring 2021 Internship Application." Include your preferred start and end date. No calls or drop-ins.

description: Representative Susie Lee's office seeks a legislative fellow to assist with member's work on appropriations committee. An emphasis will be placed on candidates who have experience working on environmental and energy policy. Responsibilities include working with Legislative Director and Legislative Assistants to develop and implement policy goals and objectives. Specific tasks include monitoring legislative developments, introducing legislation, and staffing the Congresswoman in committee hearings. The fellow will also be responsible for interacting and communicating with outside stakeholder groups within the context of the Congresswoman's legislative agenda. This includes staffing policy-oriented meetings on behalf of the office. The ideal candidate is collaborative, creative, energetic, detail-oriented, able to multi-task, politically astute, and willing to work in a fast-paced and demanding setting. Applicants should be able to start immediately and commit through May/June. This is a paid opportunity.
responsibilities: Working with Legislative Director and Legislative Assistants to develop and implement policy goals and objectives
Staffing the Congresswoman in committee hearings
Interacting and communicating with outside stakeholder groups within the context of the Congresswoman's legislative agenda
Staffing policy-oriented meetings on behalf of the office
qualifications: Experience working on environmental and energy policy (emphasis)
Collaborative, creative, energetic, and detail-oriented
Able to multi-task
Politically astute
Willing to work in a fast-paced and demanding setting
Able to start immediately and commit through May/June
how_to_apply: Submit a cover letter, resume, two writing samples, and two references to NV03Resumes@gmail.com with "Legislative Fellow Application" and the first and last name in the subject line. Please submit the cover letter, resume, and two references as one document.
equal_opportunity: The office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, national origin, disability, military status, age, marital status, or parental status.

description: Republican Ranking Member of the Energy and Commerce Committee subcommittee on Environment and Climate seeks unpaid graduate intern/fellow. Duties include performing research, staffing the congressman at hearings, writing memos and op-eds, helping to formulate legislation, and stakeholder outreach. The ideal candidate will have significant knowledge of environmental/climate change policies as well as energy policies. This is not an internship for an undergrad. This position requires significant knowledge of research and policy. Internship duration and hours are flexible. Interested candidate please email a resume along with a relevant writing sample to Kirsten Wing at Kirsten.Wing@mail.house.gov. With Subject Line "Environment Fellow Application Last Name".
qualifications: Significant knowledge of environmental/climate change policies
Significant knowledge of energy policies
Significant knowledge of research and policy
Must be a graduate student; this is not an internship for an undergraduate
how_to_apply: Email a resume along with a relevant writing sample to Kirsten.Wing@mail.house.gov with the subject line "Environment Fellow Application Last Name".

description: The Democratic staff of the House Committee on the Judiciary is seeking a digital intern for a spring position. This digital internship program includes the production of high-quality graphics, videos, and demonstratives, as well as rapid response work, post production editing, and livestreaming hybrid/virtual hearings and events. The House Committee on the Judiciary's Democratic staff internship program will be providing stipends to spring interns, with additional funds provided to interns with additional demonstrated financial need. COVID-19 update: Currently, some of our spring internship program will be conducted remotely. However, we ask that all applicants be available to intern in Washington, D.C., as some tasks will be done on site.
responsibilities: Production of high-quality graphics, videos, and demonstratives
qualifications: Strong technical skills
Advanced creativity
High level of attention to detail
Experience in Webex, OBS, Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator, Premier Pro, After Effects, LightRoom, InDesign, and Audition a plus
Experience in HTML, CSS, hard-skills technology and big-data analytics a serious plus
Must be a team player and have a strong work ethic
Willingness to take initiative, generate creative ideas, and ability to work under deadline pressure
how_to_apply: Email portfolio and resume to JudPress.Intern@mail.house.gov with DIGITAL INTERN in the subject line. Digital portfolio, including design and technical work, must be included to be considered for the position.
equal_opportunity: The Committee does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including marital or parental status, sexual orientation, and gender identity), disability, age, or national origin.

description: The House Judiciary Committee Democratic staff are looking for interns for the summer semester. The House Committee on the Judiciary's staff internship program offers undergraduate students, law students, graduate students, and recent graduates an opportunity to experience the operation of a congressional committee firsthand and learn about the important role that our Committee plays in the legislative process. The Judiciary Committee has jurisdiction over a wide range of legislative and oversight issues, including oversight of the U.S. Department of Justice, constitutional law, federal criminal law, voting rights, immigration and naturalization, intellectual property law, and antitrust law. Intern assignments will vary depending on the work of the Judiciary Committee each semester. The committee will be providing stipends to summer interns. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic the Committee is currently planning on having a remote internship for the summer of 2021. However, public health developments could necessitate the return of an in-person internship in Washington, D.C.
responsibilities: Researching policy issues under the committee's jurisdiction
Attending briefings and hearings on the Hill
Supporting committee clerks and professional staff members
Providing administrative support, including answering calls, delivering correspondence, and setting up the hearing room
qualifications: Must be an undergraduate student, law student, graduate student, or recent graduate
Must be available to intern in Washington, D.C. if it is safe to do so
how_to_apply: Apply at https://judiciary.house.gov/about/internship-opportunities.htm. The deadline to apply for the summer semester is February 15, 2021.
equal_opportunity: The Committee does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including marital or parental status, sexual orientation, and gender identity), disability, age, or national origin.

position_title: Intern, Subcommittee on Crime, Terrorism, and Homeland Security
description: The House Judiciary Committee Democratic staff are looking for an intern to work with the Crime, Terrorism, and Homeland Security subcommittee this spring, with an ideal start date of early February. The House Committee on the Judiciary's staff internship program offers undergraduate students, law students, graduate students, and recent graduates an opportunity to experience the operation of a congressional committee firsthand and learn about the important role that our Committee plays in the legislative process. The Subcommittee on Crime, Terrorism, and Homeland Security has jurisdiction over the Federal Criminal Code, drug enforcement, sentencing, parole and pardons, internal and homeland security, the Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure, prisons, and criminal law enforcement. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic the Committee is currently working virtually. However, public health developments could necessitate the return of an in-person internship in Washington, D.C.
responsibilities: Researching policy issues under the committee's jurisdiction
Attending briefings and hearings on the Hill
Supporting committee clerks and professional staff members
Providing administrative support, including answering calls, delivering correspondence, and setting up the hearing room
qualifications: Must be an undergraduate student, law student, graduate student, or recent graduate
Must be available to intern in Washington, D.C. if it is safe to do so
Strong research and writing skills
Interest in criminal law, homeland security, and related policy areas
how_to_apply: Submit a one-page resume, one-page cover letter (including pronouns, ideal start and end dates, and availability to work each weekday), writing sample, and a short statement (no more than 500 words) detailing how your lived experience will enhance your ability to contribute to this committee, to HJC.Internship@mail.house.gov with the subject line "Crime Subcommittee Internship". Applications will be accepted on a rolling basis.
equal_opportunity: The Committee does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including marital or parental status, sexual orientation, and gender identity), disability, age, or national origin.
